blocks.text:
# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |

But `cachedSet` is derived from `items` (queryPrs items) which use `prNumber` — so `labelHoldersOf(items)` pushes `it.number` = undefined for the cached derive.

Wait, in `rederiveHoldersLive`:
- `liveHolderSet = derive(mutexHoldersOf(liveItems, q), liveItems, ...)` — holders arg is numbers (from mutexHoldersOf which maps p.number — liveItems have number since normalized). liveItems have `.number`. OK.
- `cachedSet = derive(holders, items, ...)` — `holders` here is the array of item objects (from `items.filter(holdsMutex)`), and `items` are queryPrs items with `prNumber` (no `.number`). So `uniquePositive(holders)` — objects without `.number` but with `.prNumber` — holderFromObject checks `h.prNumber !== undefined` first → OK, normalizes fine.

But `labelHoldersOf(items)` — items have labels and `prNumber`, NOT `number`. So `out.push(it.number)` pushes `undefined`. Then in `derive`: `labelHolders = [undefined]`; `merged = uniquePositive(cand.concat([undefined]))` → just cand. `setOf(labelHolders)` = `{undefined: true}`. In `liveHoldersOf`: for each n in merged: `labelSet[n]` — for a real holder n, `labelSet[n]` is undefined → falsy → phantom! So a legit cached holder (label still present in cached items) reads as NOT in the label layer → phantom → spurious self-heal + cache drop + alarm every tick when a legit holder exists.

Conversely, when the live layer is clean (phantom case), cached holders [X] where X is an item whose labels DO include ai_validating in the cached view... wait in the phantom incident, the cached items still show the label (stale cache). - holders = [itemX].
- phantomHealIfFull: holders.length (1) >= mutexMax (1) → rederiveHoldersLive.

- liveHolderSet = derive([], liveItems): labelHoldersOf(liveItems) → items have .number → []. holders = []. Good.
- cachedSet = derive([itemX], items): labelHoldersOf(items) → pushes it.number = undefined → [undefined]. cand = uniquePositive([itemX]) = [X]. merged = [X]. labelSet = {undefined: true}. liveHoldersOf: n=X: labelSet[X] falsy → candSet[X] true → phantoms=[X], not holder. So cachedSet.holders = [], phantoms=[X].

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 14
- **Additions**: +1379
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T08:09:48Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1017._

> ℹ️ **8 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 298

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` line 51

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: E3 gap — a re-cancelled re-dispatch re-wedges the arm silently**

The once-per-head marker makes the ghost re-dispatch strictly one-shot per head: if the fresh CI run the machine dispatches here gets cancelled again (the gh-748 kicker race is not guaranteed to be gone — the incident that spawned this card was a cancel storm), the next tick finds `ghostProbe.isGhostCancel && ghostGateHeld` true, sees the marker, and takes this branch…

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017

- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 14
- **Additions**: +1379
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T08:09:48Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

Now I understand the flow. The reported bug: `mutexRegistry.labelHoldersOf` pushes `it.number`. In `rederiveHoldersLive`, `liveItems` are normalized to `{number, labels}` so `.number` works there. But `cachedSet` is derived from `items` (queryPrs items) which use `prNumber` — so `labelHoldersOf(items)` pushes `it.number` = undefined for the cached derive.

Wait, in `rederiveHoldersLive`:
- `liveHolderSet = derive(mutexHoldersOf(liveItems, q), liveItems, ...)` — holders arg is numbers (from mutexHoldersOf which maps p.number — liveItems have number since normalized). liveItems have `.number`. OK.
- `cachedSet = derive(holders, items, ...)` — `holders` here is the array of item objects (from `items.filter(holdsMutex)`), and `items` are queryPrs items with `prNumber` (no `.number`). So `uniquePositive(holders)` — objects without `.number` but with `.prNumber` — holderFromObject checks `h.prNumber !== undefined` first → OK, normalizes fine.

But `labelHoldersOf(items)` — items have labels and `prNumber`, NOT `number`. So `out.push(it.number)` pushes `undefined`. Then in `derive`: `labelHolders = [undefined]`; `merged = uniquePositive(cand.concat([undefined]))` → just cand. `setOf(labelHolders)` = `{undefined: true}`. In `liveHoldersOf`: for each n in merged: `labelSet[n]` — for a real holder n, `labelSet[n]` is undefined → falsy → phantom! So a legit cached holder (label still present in cached items) reads as NOT in the label layer → phantom → spurious self-heal + cache drop + alarm every tick when a legit holder exists.

Conversely, when the live layer is clean (phantom case), cached holders [X] where X is an item whose labels DO include ai_validating in the cached view... wait in the phantom incident, the cached items still show the label (stale cache). Hmm. Actually the incident: registry says 1/1 but labels say none — the cached open-PR list is stale (holder vanished from live labels). In the repro described: "query with live arm removed → candidate arms but dropped=[] and no alarm". 

Let me think about the phantom case with the current buggy code:
- cached items: PR X with labels [ai_validating] (stale cache), candidate PR Y.
- holders = [itemX].
- phantomHealIfFull: holders.length (1) >= mutexMax (1) → rederiveHoldersLive.
- liveItems from provider.listOpenPrsLive(): PR X without ai_validating, PR Y without. normalized {number, labels}.
- liveHolderSet = derive([], liveItems): labelHoldersOf(liveItems) → items have .number → []. holders = []. Good.
- cachedSet = derive([itemX], items): labelHoldersOf(items) → pushes it.number = undefined → [undefined]. cand = uniquePositive([itemX]) = [X]. merged = [X]. labelSet = {undefined: true}. liveHoldersOf: n=X: labelSet[X] falsy → candSet[X] true → phantoms=[X], not holder. So cachedSet.holders = [], phantoms=[X].
- reconcile(cachedSet=[], liveHolderSet=[]) — wait reconcile compares holders arrays: cached = [], live = [] → no divergence → noDivergenceResult → selfHealed = false! So NO alarm, NO self-heal event, but holders corrected to [] anyway (return liveHolderSet.holders = []). The candidate arms (since holders.length 0 < mutexMax), but there's no alarm/counters — I2 violated. That matches the repro: "candidate arms but dropped=[] and no alarm".

And the legit-holder case: cached items show X armed, live also shows X armed:
- liveHolderSet.holders = [X]. cachedSet.holders = [] (X reads as phantom due to undefined label set). reconcile: cached [] vs live [X] → diverge → self-heal! spurious ioCache drop + phantom alarm every tick. That's the false-diverge.

So the fix: `labelHoldersOf` should use `normalizeHolder(it)` instead of `it.number`. That fixes both directions:
- Phantom case: cachedSet.holders = [X] (X labeled in cached items, .prNumber normalized) vs live [] → diverge → self-heal + alarm. 
- Legit case: cachedSet.holders = [X], live [X] → no divergence.

if (labels.indexOf('ai_validating') !== -1) out.push(normalizeHolder(it));
```

Hmm — but for the log, using `divergent.alarm.holders.cached` vs `.live` would be ideal, since the alarm record already holds normalized cached/live. function logPhantomHeal(alarm) {

}
```

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

blocks.text:
# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |

Now I understand the flow. The reported bug: `mutexRegistry.labelHoldersOf` pushes `it.number`. In `rederiveHoldersLive`, `liveItems` are normalized to `{number, labels}` so `.number` works there. But `cachedSet` is derived from `items` (queryPrs items) which use `prNumber` — so `labelHoldersOf(items)` pushes `it.number` = undefined for the cached derive.

Wait, in `rederiveHoldersLive`:
- `liveHolderSet = derive(mutexHoldersOf(liveItems, q), liveItems, ...)` — holders arg is numbers (from mutexHoldersOf which maps p.number — liveItems have number since normalized). liveItems have `.number`. OK.
- `cachedSet = derive(holders, items, ...)` — `holders` here is the array of item objects (from `items.filter(holdsMutex)`), and `items` are queryPrs items with `prNumber` (no `.number`). So `uniquePositive(holders)` — objects without `.number` but with `.prNumber` — holderFromObject checks `h.prNumber !== undefined` first → OK, normalizes fine.

But `labelHoldersOf(items)` — items have labels and `prNumber`, NOT `number`. So `out.push(it.number)` pushes `undefined`. Then in `derive`: `labelHolders = [undefined]`; `merged = uniquePositive(cand.concat([undefined]))` → just cand. `setOf(labelHolders)` = `{undefined: true}`. In `liveHoldersOf`: for each n in merged: `labelSet[n]` — for a real holder n, `labelSet[n]` is undefined → falsy → phantom! So a legit cached holder (label still present in cached items) reads as NOT in the label layer → phantom → spurious self-heal + cache drop + alarm every tick when a legit holder exists.

Conversely, when the live layer is clean (phantom case), cached holders [X] where X is an item whose labels DO include ai_validating in the cached view... wait in the phantom incident, the cached items still show the label (stale cache). Hmm. Actually the incident: registry says 1/1 but labels say none — the cached open-PR list is stale (holder vanished from live labels). In the repro described: "query with live arm removed → candidate arms but dropped=[] and no alarm". 

Let me think about the phantom case with the current buggy code:
- cached items: PR X with labels [ai_validating] (stale cache), candidate PR Y.
- holders = [itemX].
- phantomHealIfFull: holders.length (1) >= mutexMax (1) → rederiveHoldersLive.
- liveItems from provider.listOpenPrsLive(): PR X without ai_validating, PR Y without. normalized {number, labels}.
- liveHolderSet = derive([], liveItems): labelHoldersOf(liveItems) → items have .number → []. holders = []. Good.
- cachedSet = derive([itemX], items): labelHoldersOf(items) → pushes it.number = undefined → [undefined]. cand = uniquePositive([itemX]) = [X]. merged = [X]. labelSet = {undefined: true}. liveHoldersOf: n=X: labelSet[X] falsy → candSet[X] true → phantoms=[X], not holder. So cachedSet.holders = [], phantoms=[X].
- reconcile(cachedSet=[], liveHolderSet=[]) — wait reconcile compares holders arrays: cached = [], live = [] → no divergence → noDivergenceResult → selfHealed = false! So NO alarm, NO self-heal event, but holders corrected to [] anyway (return liveHolderSet.holders = []). The candidate arms (since holders.length 0 < mutexMax), but there's no alarm/counters — I2 violated. That matches the repro: "candidate arms but dropped=[] and no alarm".

And the legit-holder case: cached items show X armed, live also shows X armed:
- liveHolderSet.holders = [X]. cachedSet.holders = [] (X reads as phantom due to undefined label set). reconcile: cached [] vs live [X] → diverge → self-heal! spurious ioCache drop + phantom alarm every tick. That's the false-diverge.

So the fix: `labelHoldersOf` should use `normalizeHolder(it)` instead of `it.number`. That fixes both directions:
- Phantom case: cachedSet.holders = [X] (X labeled in cached items, .prNumber normalized) vs live [] → diverge → self-heal + alarm. 
- Legit case: cachedSet.holders = [X], live [X] → no divergence.

if (labels.indexOf('ai_validating') !== -1) out.push(normalizeHolder(it));
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 14
- **Additions**: +1379
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T08:09:48Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1017._

> ℹ️ **8 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 298

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` line 51

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

But `cachedSet` is derived from `items` (queryPrs items) which use `prNumber` — so `labelHoldersOf(items)` pushes `it.number` = undefined for the cached derive.

Wait, in `rederiveHoldersLive`:
- `liveHolderSet = derive(mutexHoldersOf(liveItems, q), liveItems, ...)` — holders arg is numbers (from mutexHoldersOf which maps p.number — liveItems have number since normalized). liveItems have `.number`. OK.
- `cachedSet = derive(holders, items, ...)` — `holders` here is the array of item objects (from `items.filter(holdsMutex)`), and `items` are queryPrs items with `prNumber` (no `.number`). So `uniquePositive(holders)` — objects without `.number` but with `.prNumber` — holderFromObject checks `h.prNumber !== undefined` first → OK, normalizes fine.

But `labelHoldersOf(items)` — items have labels and `prNumber`, NOT `number`. So `out.push(it.number)` pushes `undefined`. In `liveHoldersOf`: for each n in merged: `labelSet[n]` — for a real holder n, `labelSet[n]` is undefined → falsy → phantom! So a legit cached holder (label still present in cached items) reads as NOT in the label layer → phantom → spurious self-heal + cache drop + alarm every tick when a legit holder exists.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 14
- **Additions**: +1379
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T08:09:48Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).
